name: StandardAero, Inc.
business: StandardAero sells aircraft engine maintenance, repair and overhaul plus component repair services to commercial airlines, military and business aviation operators.

events.what: New CEO succeeding retiring Chairman and CEO Russell Ford (CEO since October 2013); becomes Chairman 2027-01-01, Ford Executive Chairman through 2026-12-31
events.from: Lead independent director since the 2024 IPO; Senior Operating Partner, AE Industrial Partners; 30-year GE career incl. CEO of GE Aviation Services and GE Power Services

events.what: Chief Operating Officer departs; stays employed to support leadership transition until 2026-12-31
New President, Component Repair Services, succeeding Kimberly Ashmun
Chairman transition from Russell Ford to Paul McElhinney (pending)
Bolt-on acquisition of Unified Turbines (CRS hot-section repair), closed Q2 2026; no 8-K Item 1.01 or 2.01 filed, so not material
events.source: Q2 2026 Earnings Call, Dan Satterfield, 2026-08-06, document_id 130389

next_event.source: Lexical 'investor day' search over FY2026 corpus (cid 1005763) returned no hits. The next scheduled touchpoint is the Q3 2026 earnings call, the new CEO's first; date not yet announced in Baba (Q3 2025 call was held 2025-11-10, document_id 52873).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: The only consolidated level is a one-year guide: about 14% for 2026 (CFO, 2026-02-25), with EBITDA guide since raised to $885M to $910M on $6.375B to $6.5B revenue (2026-08-06). The annual rate (40 to 50 bps a year historically, lately closer to 80 bps) is an Engine Services segment figure stated by the SVP of Investor Relations as history, not a forward target. The $25M license EBITDA (2029) is an incremental contribution at accretive margins, not a savings figure. No multi-year consolidated margin target exists; the new CEO has not spoken publicly as CEO.

statements.quote: For full year 2026, we expect total company Adjusted EBITDA of $870-$905 million, or approximately 10% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This implies a 70 basis point margin improvement year-over-year to about 14%.
statements.speaker: Dan Satterfield

statements.quote: We've historically, over the last 10 years, have done about 40 to 50 basis points of margin improvement in Engine Services organically through continuous improvement. Lately, it's been closer to 80 basis points. We expect to see continued growth from the margin, primarily from that.
statements.speaker: Rama Bondada

statements.quote: We expect the license to add $10 million of adjusted EBITDA in 2027, $20 million in 2028, and $25 million annually in 2029 and beyond.
statements.speaker: Dan Satterfield

statements.quote: Component repair, will it max out at 30%? I don't know, right? They can probably do better as, you know, the insourcing effort is pure margin, right?
statements.speaker: Dan Satterfield

street.gap_assumption: December fiscal year, so VA labels equal company fiscal years. Compares the CFO's about 14% 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guide with VA FY2026 consensus (901.2M / 6,457.2M = 13.96%). The street then models about 56 bps and 41 bps of further expansion (14.51% FY2027, 14.92% FY2028), in line with the 40 to 50 bps historical Engine Services rate IR cites. Only if the 'lately closer to 80 bps' pace were applied to the whole company from 14% would FY2028 sit about 70 bps above the street; management has not said that.
street.source: Baba data_financials summary consensus (Visible Alpha) cid 1005763; margins and gap via data_compute

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026: VA EBITDA 203.2M on 1,626.9M revenue (12.49%) vs Q1 2025 13.81%, -132 bps (CFO had flagged a CRS hit from the US government shutdown spillover and a Phoenix CRS facility fire). Q2 2026: adjusted EBITDA margin 14.4%, +100 bps yoy, a record, per 8-K EX-99.1 0002025410-26-000007 (document_id 143912); VA has not loaded the Q2 2026 actual. LTM 13.26% uses VA 3Q25 to 1Q26 plus the Q2 2026 8-K actual. Drawdown is from data_profile pct_off_52w_high (-35.5%, high $33.12, price $21.17 on 2026-10-01) because data_comps drawdown is null for a stock listed 2024-10-02.

verdict: Cheap, broken post-IPO stock with a CEO from outside management one day in seat and a COO exit, but the only numeric margin frame (about 14% in 2026) is already in consensus; the setup depends on what McElhinney says on his first call.
open_questions: Does McElhinney's first call (Q3 2026, date not yet set) bring a multi-year consolidated margin target, and does it sit at least 100 bps above the 14.92% FY2028 consensus?
Why did COO Kimberly Ernzen leave three days before the CEO change, and is an external COO or new operating team coming?
Is the CRS margin dip (26.3% in Q2 2026, down 270 bps) temporary, given the military input delays and labor ramp?
